title: Ezekiel Acts Out the Exile

questions.question: The word of the Lord came to Ezekiel: "Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, who have eyes to see, but see not, who have ears to hear, but hear not, for they are..."
options: A rebellious house
Blind and deaf
A stiff-necked people
Dead in their sins
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:2 (ESV): "who have eyes to see, but see not, who have ears to hear, but hear not, for they are a rebellious house."

questions.question: What was Ezekiel instructed to prepare for himself by day in their sight?
options: Baggage for exile
A large feast
A suit of armor
A scroll of lamentation
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:3 (ESV): "As for you, son of man, prepare for yourself baggage for exile, and go into exile by day in their sight."

questions.question: In the evening, when he was "going into exile," what was Ezekiel told to do to the wall of his house in their sight?
options: Dig through it
Paint it red
Burn it down
Pour water over it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:5 (ESV): "In their sight dig through the wall, and bring your baggage out through it."

questions.question: How was Ezekiel specifically supposed to carry his baggage and cover his face as he went out in the dark?
options: He was to shoulder it in the dark, and cover his face so he could not see the land
He was to drag it behind him in chains
He was to carry it on his head while weeping loudly
He was to ride on a donkey blindfolded
questions.correctAnswer: He was to shoulder it in the dark, and cover his face so he could not see the land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:6 (ESV): "In their sight you shall lift the baggage upon your shoulder and carry it out in the dark. You shall cover your face that you may not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel."

questions.question: Who did God say the oracle applied to?
options: The prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel in it
The exiles already in Babylon
The king of Babylon and his armies
The false prophets in Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel in it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:10 (ESV): "Say to them, 'Thus says the Lord God: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in it.'"

questions.question: What prophecy was given about the prince who is among them regarding his journey?
options: He shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder in the dark... He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes
He shall ride out in glory and triumph
He shall be carried in a golden chariot to Egypt
He shall swim across the Jordan secretly
questions.correctAnswer: He shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder in the dark... He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:12 (ESV): "And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder in the dark and shall go out. He shall dig through the wall to bring it out through it. He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes."

questions.question: What will God spread over the prince, and bring him to Babylon in Chaldea, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there?
options: His net
His shadow
The wings of an eagle
A thick darkness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:13 (ESV): "And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare. And I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there." (Zedekiah was blinded before going to Babylon, fulfilling this perfectly).

questions.question: What will God do to all the prince's helpers and troops?
options: Scatter them to every wind and unsheathe the sword after them
Make them serve the king of Babylon willingly
Feed them to the birds of the air
Strike them with a plague of blindness
questions.correctAnswer: Scatter them to every wind and unsheathe the sword after them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:14 (ESV): "And I will scatter toward every wind all who are around him, his helpers and all his troops, and I will unsheathe the sword after them."

questions.question: Why does God say He will let a few of them escape from the sword, from famine, and pestilence?
options: That they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they go
So that a remnant of the royal line would not be cut off completely
Because He remembered His covenant with David
To show the Babylonians His mercy
questions.correctAnswer: That they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they go
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:16 (ESV): "But I will let a few of them escape from the sword, from famine and pestilence, that they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they go..."

questions.question: What physical sign was Ezekiel told to do when he ate his bread and drank his water?
options: Eat with quaking, and drink water with trembling and with anxiety
Eat it standing up, with his staff in his hand
Drink it mixed with ashes
Eat it lying on his side
questions.correctAnswer: Eat with quaking, and drink water with trembling and with anxiety
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:18 (ESV): "Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink water with trembling and with anxiety."

questions.question: What does eating with anxiety and quaking symbolize for the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: They shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink water in dismay... because of the violence of all who dwell in it
It represents the great earthquake that will strike them
It represents the fear of foreign plagues
It symbolizes their terror of false prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink water in dismay... because of the violence of all who dwell in it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:19 (ESV): "They shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink water in dismay. In this way her land will be stripped of all it contains, on account of the violence of all those who dwell in it."

questions.question: What proverb did the people of Israel have about prophecies taking a long time? "The days grow long, and..."
options: Every vision comes to nothing
The Lord forgets his words
The prophets slumber in sleep
The peace of the land remains
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:22 (ESV): "Son of man, what is this proverb that you have about the land of Israel, saying, 'The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing'?"

questions.question: What did God say would happen to that proverb?
options: "I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel."
"I will make it a reality for them."
"It will be inscribed on their tombs."
"I will laugh at their proverb."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:23 (ESV): "Tell them therefore, 'Thus says the Lord God: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel.'"

questions.question: "For there shall be no more any... or... divination within the house of Israel."
options: False vision / flattering
True dreamer / lying
Prophet / dark
Oracle / deceitful
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:24 (ESV): "For there shall be no more any false vision or flattering divination within the house of Israel."

questions.question: Some in the house of Israel said, "The vision that he sees is for many days from now, and he prophesies of times far off." How did God respond?
options: "None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed,"
"They speak the truth, but it will come to pass,"
"They will live long enough to see it fail,"
"The times are known only to Me."
questions.correctAnswer: "None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed,"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:28 (ESV): "Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord God: None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord God."

key_verse_text: "Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord God: None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord God."
